newsitem.title: DUBAI: BP Oman petchem study ready in September.
newsitem.headline: BP Oman petchem study ready in September.

text.p: British Petroleum Co Plc is expected to complete a feasibility study in September on a planned $900 million petrochemical plant in the Gulf Arab state of Oman, a BP spokesman said on Wednesday.
"The feasibility study is still underway. There has been some delay to it but it is expected to be completed in September," a BP spokesman in London said.
Oman in November named BP Chemicals as its foreign partner in a petrochemical plant capable of producing 450,000 tonnes a year of ethylene and polyethylene.

The main focus of the study, which was due for completion in July, concerns the supply of gas to the plant at Sohar, 200 km (125 miles) north of the Omani capital Muscat, and the development of a fully fledged port at Sohar.
The plant, the first major petrochemical facility in the country, is expected to come on stream between 2001-2002.
Equity arrangements still have to be finalised though BP are expected to take a 40-49 percent stake.
